chunks: Ahmad ibn Idris and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan, from Amr ibn Saeed, from Musaddaq ibn Sadaqa, from Ammar al-Sabati, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
A man cuts his hair with his teeth; should he wipe it with water before he prays? He (peace be upon him) said: There is no problem. Rather, that is regarding (cutting it with) the iron.

key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no problem / it is permissible

ai.seo_question: Does cutting hair with teeth break wudu or require wiping with water before prayer?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies a nuance in ritual purity by distinguishing between natural hair removal and artificial cutting; Imam al-Sadiq (AS) rules that hair cut with teeth does not require wiping (masah) before prayer, reserving that requirement for hair cut with iron tools. This distinction highlights the Shia scholarly focus on the material cause of impurity or alteration, emphasizing that the physical presence of the tool (iron) triggers the specific purification act rather than the mere removal of hair. It serves as a practical guideline for worshippers to maintain wudu validity without unnecessary ritual burden.
